summary: Focused re-verification of the iter_5 critical bug: GET /api/reports/{report_id}.pdf 500/KeyError 'party_name' for invoice-kind reports. Fix at server.py:1605 (`rep.get('party_name') or rep.get('kind') or 'steeltrack'`) is now VERIFIED. Ran only the focused slice requested: TestInvoicePdf (iter_5, 3 existing + 1 added) and TestReportsStatement (iter_3 party-statement, 6 tests). Result: 10/10 PASS. Full flow (office PATCHes /entries/{id}/office with invoice_no+party_name+rate → POST /entries/{id}/invoice-pdf → GET download_url) returns 200 application/pdf with %PDF- body — no 500. Download also works via main JWT (Authorization: Bearer) in addition to signed ?token=. Content-Disposition filename contains a safe fallback ('invoice' from rep['kind']) when party_name is not stored on the report doc, confirming no KeyError. Party-statement flow continues to work and still embeds party_name in the Content-Disposition filename via the same `rep.get('party_name')` branch. No regression in party-statement download. The iter_5 iteration_5 blocker is resolved.

minor.issue: Filename template is now safe but still contains the literal '-statement-' infix for ALL report kinds, so invoice downloads come out as 'invoice-statement-<id>.pdf' which reads oddly. Cosmetic only; recommend branching on rep.get('kind') (e.g. 'invoice-<id>.pdf' vs '<party>-statement-<id>.pdf') for cleaner UX. Not blocking.

(Carried from iter_5) Still does NOT persist invoice_no / party_name on the db.reports doc. The download now works via fallback, but admin / audit queries can't filter invoice reports by party_name or invoice number. Suggest storing those fields in the insert_one at server.py ~1772 so filenames can also stay informative.

action_items: (Optional cosmetic) server.py:1605 — branch filename on rep.get('kind'): 'invoice-<id>.pdf' for kind=='invoice' vs '<party>-statement-<id>.pdf' for party-statement reports. Current string reads 'invoice-statement-xxxxx.pdf' which works but is awkward.
(Carried) Persist invoice_no + party_name on db.reports when kind='invoice' (server.py ~1772) for admin queries and better filenames.

(Carried from iter_5) Migrate /app/backend/tests/test_steeltrack_iter3_features.py::TestParties::test_parties_sorted_deduplicated to the new object-shape /parties contract (not retested here per scoped request).
(Carried) server.py is 1832 lines — still 2.6x over the 700-line soft cap. Modularise into routers before adding new features.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix verified at /app/backend/server.py:1605 — Content-Disposition now uses `rep.get('party_name') or rep.get('kind') or 'steeltrack'` which eliminates the KeyError for invoice reports (where party_name is not stored). Fallback chain is correct and safe.

RBAC path is unchanged: owner-of-report (via signed ?token= scoped to report_id) OR admin/office with main JWT both reach the response branch — both paths now succeed for invoice reports (newly added regression test test_invoice_pdf_download_via_main_jwt_also_works confirms the Authorization-header path).

No change needed to POST /entries/{id}/invoice-pdf for correctness — the fix is pure read-side. However persisting party_name there would make filenames informative (currently they fall back to 'invoice').

rca_of_issue: ORIGINAL: GET /api/reports/{id}.pdf 500 KeyError 'party_name' when kind='invoice'. ROOT CAUSE: download_report built the Content-Disposition filename as rep['party_name'], but POST /entries/{id}/invoice-pdf inserts only {id,path,owner_id,entry_id,kind:'invoice',created_at} into db.reports — party_name is only persisted by party-statement. FIX APPLIED (confirmed in server.py:1605): `f'inline; filename="{rep.get("party_name") or rep.get("kind") or "steeltrack"}-statement-{report_id[:8]}.pdf"'`. VERIFICATION: 10 focused tests pass; download returns 200/application/pdf with %PDF- body and filename containing 'invoice' fallback for invoice reports or the actual party name for party-statement reports.
